question.text: $f(x)=\sin x+\cos x, g(x)=x^2-1$, then $g(f(x))$ is invertible if

solution.text: Given that, $f(x)=\sin x+\cos x$ $g(x)=x^2-1$ $g[f(x)]=(\sin x+\cos x)^2-1$ $=\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x+2 \sin x \cos x-1$ $=1+\sin 2 x-1=\sin 2 x$ $\left(\because \sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x=1, \sin x=2 \sin x \cos x\right)$ Among the given options, $\sin 2 x$ is monotonous (here strictly increasing) in $-\frac{\pi}{4} \leq x \leq \frac{\pi}{4}$. So, $g(f(x))$ is invertible in $-\frac{\pi}{4} \leq x \leq \frac{\pi}{4}$.
